This is implemented by applying the 1D pyramidal algorithm sequentially along the principal axes.
Create an index volume $I$ with the same resolution as the spatial volume.
For each pixel, cast a ray through the volume.
Initialize the ray position and step size.
Sample the spatial volume $V$ at the new position.
Composite the sample into the pixel buffer (e.g., using front-to-back compositing).
*   **Memory Overhead:** The index volume requires approximately 3 bytes (or 4 bits) per voxel.
*   **Reconstruction Cost:** The index volume must be reconstructed whenever the error bound $E$ changes.
*   **On-the-fly Reconstruction Avoidance:** Direct evaluation in the wavelet domain is expensive due to the large number of coefficients required for reconstruction.
